title: Network-Offloaded Bandwidth-Optimal Broadcast and Allgather for Distributed AI
event_hint: Bandwidth-optimal Allgather built on a hardware-multicast constant-time reliable Broadcast and offloaded to SmartNIC, halving collective traffic and targeting next-gen 1.6 Tbit/s links.
problem: In Fully Sharded Data Parallel (FSDP) training, collective operations (Allgather and Reduce-Scatter) are interleaved to maximize communication overlap, but they compete for injection bandwidth and create pipeline bubbles. Standard Allgather is not bandwidth-optimal and host-based progress consumes CPU.
mechanism: Proposes a bandwidth-optimal Allgather collective that leverages hardware multicast. A constant-time reliable Broadcast protocol is built from multicast as the composing primitive. The collective progress engine is offloaded to a SmartNIC, decoupling collective progress from the host and enabling scaling to next-generation high-bandwidth links.

evidence.claim: The Allgather algorithm achieves 2x traffic reduction on a 188-node testbed.
SmartNIC-offloaded collective progress engine can scale to next-generation 1.6 Tbit/s links.
Uses hardware multicast to build a constant-time reliable Broadcast protocol as the building block for the bandwidth-optimal Allgather.
In FSDP, outstanding operations such as Allgather and Reduce-Scatter compete for injection bandwidth and create pipeline bubbles.

evaluation_context: 188-node testbed; FSDP-style collectives (Allgather, Reduce-Scatter); SmartNIC offload; demonstrated scaling toward 1.6 Tbit/s links.
limitations: Abstract-level; detailed microbenchmarks (latency curves, CPU-offload savings, comparison to other offload targets like DPUs/GPUs) require full text. Hardware-multicast availability is assumed (network must support it). Full body not fetched.
project_relevance: Directly relevant to DPU/SmartNIC offload: it demonstrates moving collective progress onto a SmartNIC and reaching bandwidth-optimal Allgather via hardware multicast, a concrete template for offloading training/inference-network collectives onto network hardware. The 1.6 Tbit/s scaling target aligns with the next-gen fabric roadmap; adjacent to KVCache cross-node transfer concerns.
